description: An erect, open, grey-barked shrub or small tree 2-6 m tall whose small, dark green, wedge-shaped leaves are toothed at the tip and crowded on short spur shoots; in summer it is hung with long, twisted, silver-plumed seed tails that catch the light. It grows on rocky chaparral slopes, canyon walls and in foothill pine woodland, and it is a favourite deer browse, most of all in winter when its leaves stay on.

season_notes.winter: Most leaves stay on through a foothill winter, and deer come to browse them.
season_notes.spring: Fresh leaves on the spurs and tiny, inconspicuous yellowish flowers in March and April.
season_notes.summer: Silvery feathered tails 5-10 cm long grow from the seeds and shine against the dark leaves when the sun is behind them.
season_notes.fall: The plumes twist and drift off on the wind, drilling their seeds into the soil.

notes: Birch-leaf mountain mahogany (C. montanus var. glaber in some treatments) is an erect, open shrub or small tree, 2-6 m, of rocky chaparral, canyon walls and the drier foothill pine and oak woodland, often on thin soils and rock outcrops; it resprouts from the root crown after fire. Form: plain 'shrub' with few (2-5) upright stems (stem_spread_deg 22, an inverse-conical envelope) and an 'old' class to 6.5 m with a bare base for the small-tree form. Branching is of long shoots and short spur shoots: level 2 is many short side shoots (length_ratio 0.3) that carry the leaves in tufts, so the foliage cards are small (cluster_m 0.32) and gathered in small clumps. Bark smooth, grey, often lichened ('smooth_grey'); twigs reddish grey-brown. Leaves 1-3 cm, obovate to wedge-shaped, toothed above the middle, dark green above and paler, finely hairy beneath, with straight parallel side veins like a birch leaf: leaf_shape 'oval' at 2.5 cm, palette 20% paler for the undersides. Leaf-on: mostly evergreen at foothill elevations but it drops part of its leaves in cold winters and in drought, so leaf_on winter 0.6 and winter_twigs 0.3 (deciduous stays false). Flowers small and inconspicuous, March-April: not drawn. Fruit an achene with a twisted, feathery style 5-10 cm long that stays on the shrub through summer and silvers the whole crown in back light; the generator has no plume form, so these are drawn as 'berries' (form cluster, a pale silver-grey, size 7 cm, months 7-10): the berries block here stands for the plumed achenes, not for fruit. A valued deer browse throughout the year and especially in winter, when its leaves are still there. Architectural model Rauh (provisional): rhythmic monopodial long shoots with lateral short shoots. Lineup 2026-10-29: gaps 0.51 against 0.3, so cards_per_m2 9 and the budget 1,300.
